en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having the most perfect cone shape among all volcanoes in the world.
The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the largest and rarest eagle found only in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Babuyan Channel.
Taal Lake in Batangas is the third largest lake in the Philippines and contains Volcano Island within its waters.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse coral reefs and marine life.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates and has enormous eyes adapted for night vision.
Marine scientists call the Verde Island Passage between Batangas and Mindoro the center of the center of marine biodiversity.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago using simple hand tools.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical mounds that turn brown during the dry season, resembling chocolate kisses.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo in Zambales was the second-largest volcanic eruption of the twentieth century and created a massive caldera lake.
